While we wait for the third-quarter updates, here’s a thought: Investor enthusiasm for semiconductor stocks and blue-sky vision companies like SpaceX appears to have sucked money out of stocks of long-established tech companies. Some are now trading at bargain-basement prices. We’re thinking specifically of Amazon, whose stock really deserves a bit more love. We know the gripes: Like Alphabet and Meta, Amazon is spending an absolute ton—$220 billion this year alone—on capital expenditures to build out its AI data center capacity. That’s not without risk, for sure: The investment depends on business demand for AI services taking off. Even so, that can’t justify Amazon trading at a discount to Walmart, as it has done for the last 18 months or so. Walmart is expected to grow revenue this year by about 5.6%—about a third of Amazon’s estimated growth rate. And yet Amazon is trading at about 29 times forward earnings, compared with 37 times for Walmart, according to Koyfin data.

items.title: Former Tesla Optimus Lead is Launching an Industrial Robot Startup
items.summary: Ashish Kumar , a former AI lead for Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robots, has co-founded a startup developing non-humanoid robots that handle a variety of tasks that would normally be done by highly skilled workers in industries such as manufacturing and aerospace, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The San Francisco startup, Intelligent Machines , has hired several former members of Tesla’s Optimus team and is in the process of raising a seed round that could end up around $100 million, said one of the people.
